name: nighttime-radiance
what_it_holds: Python scripts and Jupyter notebooks to download and preprocess VIIRS DNB (Day/Night Band) nighttime-lights data from NOAA/NASA sources; no data committed, method/pipeline only.
why_useful: Lighter-weight alternative to blackmarblepy for a one-off pull of VIIRS DNB imagery over a specific tourism destination bounding box; BSD-3 licensed.
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: Lighter-weight alternative to blackmarblepy for a one-off pull of VIIRS DNB imagery over a specific tourism destination bounding box; BSD-3 licensed.

why_all: General-purpose analysis tool if the team ever works in Julia; not tourism-specific.

name: syria-economic-monitor (and sibling datapartnership/*-economic-monitor repos)
what_it_holds: World Bank Data Partnership template repo combining remote sensing (nighttime lights, port/trade activity via satellite), mobility patterns, internet connectivity, and vegetation conditions to track economic activity in data-scarce countries. Same org has near-identical repos for Niger, Algeria, Egypt, Ethiopia, Myanmar, Morocco — a reusable methodology, not Airbnb-market data itself (all current instances cover conflict/data-scarce non-ABNB markets).
why_useful: Not directly usable (wrong geographies) but is a concrete, working template for combining nightlights + mobility + connectivity into a single "economic activity monitor" — the same recipe could be forked and re-pointed at an ABNB-relevant tourism destination (e.g. a LatAm or APAC market from gap #7) faster than building from scratch.
geography: Syria, Niger, Algeria, Egypt, Ethiopia, Myanmar, Morocco (none are core ABNB markets)
time_coverage: varies by country monitor, generally recent (2023-2026)
size_hint: notebooks + processed indicator files per country repo
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: Not directly usable (wrong geographies) but is a concrete, working template for combining nightlights + mobility + connectivity into a single "economic activity monitor" — the same recipe could be forked and re-pointed at an ABNB-relevant tourism destination (e.g. a LatAm or APAC market from gap #7) faster than building from scratch.

name: nighttime-lights (DMSP deblurring)
what_it_holds: MATLAB academic replication package implementing 'Deblurring DMSP nighttime lights: A new method using Gaussian filters and Frequencies of illumination' (Abrahams et al.) — deblur_roving_window_call_script.m + block_deblur.m. No committed imagery; operates on NOAA NGDC EOG global annual DMSP composites + frequency-of-illumination rasters supplied by the user. 16 commits, 8 stars, 5 forks, MIT-licensed (citation required).
why_useful: Methods package for sharpening older, low-resolution DMSP nightlights (pre-VIIRS, i.e. pre-2012) — relevant if the team ever wants a longer/older nightlights-based tourism-activity series than VIIRS alone provides, or to make historical nightlights comparable across the DMSP/VIIRS transition.
themes: Occupancy/demand estimation from satellite, nightlights, or imagery; parking-lot counts; Sentinel-based tourism activity
why_all: Methods package for sharpening older, low-resolution DMSP nightlights (pre-VIIRS, i.e. pre-2012) — relevant if the team ever wants a longer/older nightlights-based tourism-activity series than VIIRS alone provides, or to make historical nightlights comparable across the DMSP/VIIRS transition.

name: departures-board
what_it_holds: 175-star hardware/software project (ESP32 + OLED) for a live UK rail/London Underground/bus departures board, pulling real-time feeds from National Rail, TfL, and Bustimes APIs; actively updated (Sep 2026).
why_useful: Not ridership data itself, but a maintained, working reference client for the TfL and National Rail real-time APIs (including Heathrow Express-adjacent National Rail feeds) that could be repurposed to sample live train frequency/crowding signals as a lightweight London visitor-flow proxy.
themes: Public transit ridership and airport rail links (MTA, TfL, RATP, JR) as visitor proxies; ridership open data
why_all: Not ridership data itself, but a maintained, working reference client for the TfL and National Rail real-time APIs (including Heathrow Express-adjacent National Rail feeds) that could be repurposed to sample live train frequency/crowding signals as a lightweight London visitor-flow proxy.
